name: Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North East Region (PM-DevINE)
ministry: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
agency: MDoNER (projects executed by State Governments/central agencies)
policyArea: Regional development / infrastructure / social development / livelihoods
subcategory: High-impact infrastructure and livelihood projects for NER
period: FY2022-23 to FY2025-26 (co-terminus with 15th FC); operationally continuing in FY2026-27 with a Budget 2026-27 allocation of Rs.2,300 crore and fresh Q1 FY2026-27 sanctions
whyItMatters: PM-DevINE is 100% centrally funded and takes larger, high-visibility projects than most windows open to a small state. Sikkim has already secured 5 projects worth about Rs.561 crore and is the only NE state with completed projects (including the Pelling-Sangachoeling ropeway), giving it a strong delivery track record to argue for a bigger share of the pipeline. With FY2026-27 sanctions already flowing (3 Sikkim projects, Rs.82.81 crore across MDoNER schemes in Q1), a ready shelf of DPRs positions Sikkim to capture early-cycle funding.
sikkimNodalDept: Development Planning, Economic Reforms and North Eastern Council Affairs Department (planning/nodal), with line departments (Tourism, Health, PWD) as executing agencies — likely
whatCanBeFunded: Infrastructure in the spirit of PM GatiShakti; social development projects; livelihood activities for youth and women; gap-filling in various sectors. Sikkim examples: passenger ropeways, skywalks, State Medical College at Sichey, Gyan Mandir Library Gangtok.
fundingAvailable: Scheme outlay Rs.6,600 crore (FY2022-23 to FY2025-26); Budget 2026-27 allocation Rs.2,300 crore. 48 projects worth Rs.6,044.36 crore sanctioned NER-wide till 28 February 2026. Sikkim share so far: 5 projects, approx Rs.561.11 crore.
nePreferenceDetail: Exclusively for the 8 North Eastern states including Sikkim; 100% central funding.
stateContribution: Nil capital contribution (100% central funding); State bears O&M sustainability arrangements as per project sanction — details Not confirmed from available official guidance.
accessPathway: State line department identifies a high-impact project consistent with PM-DevINE objectives (infrastructure, social sector, livelihoods)
Prepare DPR and route it through the State's planning/nodal department to MDoNER
MDoNER appraises the proposal per the August 2023 scheme guidelines (requires confirmation whether revised guidelines have been issued for the post-March 2026 period)
Approval by the scheme's empowered inter-ministerial committee chaired at MDoNER level (requires confirmation)
Sanction, fund release in instalments against physical/financial progress tracked on MDoNER's NE-Setu dashboard
nextAction: Development Planning, Economic Reforms and NECA Department should confirm with MDoNER the appraisal calendar and any revised PM-DevINE guidelines for FY2026-27 and submit 2-3 shelf-ready DPRs (e.g., disaster-resilient tourism or health infrastructure).
applicationWindow: rolling (proposal-driven; no fixed call dates announced)

name: North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme — Roads component (NESIDS-Roads)

NESIDS-Roads offers 100% central funding for roads and bridges, complementing (not duplicating) PMGSY and NH works. MDoNER's inter-ministerial facilitation has already prioritised the alternative alignment to NH-10 for Sikkim, indicating ministry-level receptiveness to Sikkim road proposals.
sikkimNodalDept: Roads and Bridges Department, Government of Sikkim (with Development Planning, ER & NECA Department as nodal) — likely

subcategory: Multi-sector projects of regional significance: connectivity, agriculture/allied, tourism, human resource development, S&T, industry

name: Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme, 2024 (UNNATI 2024)
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade - DPIIT)
subcategory: Capital investment incentive, interest subvention and manufacturing/services-linked incentives for new and expanding units in NER
period: In force 09.03.2024 to 08.03.2034 (plus 8 years for committed liabilities); unit registration window 09.03.2024 to 31.03.2026 (no extension located)
whyItMatters: UNNATI is the successor industrial-incentive regime for the NER and the main lever for attracting private manufacturing and services investment to Sikkim (pharma, food processing, tourism-linked services). Incentives flow to private units, but the State government's facilitation quality — registration support through DICs, land and clearances — determines how much of the corpus Sikkim captures. With the registration window having closed on 31 March 2026 (unless extended), the immediate state task is ensuring registered Sikkim units convert registrations into commissioned investments and claims.
eligibleApplicants: New industrial units in the 8 NE states
sikkimNodalDept: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Sikkim (with District Industries Centres and the SEED Cell)
whatCanBeFunded: Part A incentives to eligible units: Capital Investment Incentive (CII), Central Interest Subvention (CIS), and Manufacturing & Services Linked Incentive (MSLI), with zone-differentiated rates per the gazette notification; Part B for scheme administration. Minimum investment thresholds: Rs.1 crore plant & machinery (manufacturing), Rs.50 lakh (services/micro categories) per scheme documents.
fundingAvailable: Approved scheme outlay approx Rs.10,037 crore over the scheme period (as reported at March 2024 Cabinet approval); incentives are demand-driven against registrations, with disbursal capped by approved funds (registration can be halted at 115% committed liability).
fundingRatio: 100% Central (incentives paid by Government of India to units)
nePreferenceDetail: Applies only to the 8 NE states including Sikkim; zone-based differentiation gives higher incentive rates to less-industrialised districts (Zone A/B per notification).
stateContribution: None mandated for the incentive corpus; State provides facilitation, land, and single-window clearances.
accessPathway: Unit registers on the UNNATI portal (unnati.dpiit.gov.in) — window ran 09.03.2024 to 31.03.2026; any reopening/extension requires confirmation
Registered unit commences commercial production/operation within the notified period and applies for incentive claims with prescribed documentation
State-level committee scrutiny and DPIIT sanction of claims (requires confirmation of exact claim chain)
Commerce & Industries Department/DICs assist units and track claims
nextAction: Commerce and Industries Department should audit all Sikkim units registered on the UNNATI portal before 31 March 2026, fast-track their land/clearance needs so they commission within eligibility timelines, and formally query DPIIT on any registration-window extension.
applicationWindow: registration closed 31 March 2026 (per scheme notification; extension not located); incentive claims by registered units continue per scheme timelines

The State's role is ecosystem-side: sourcing and preparing investable Sikkim startups (tourism-tech, organic agri-tech) so more equity lands in the state.

name: NEDFi Financing Windows (term loans, MSME and micro-lending schemes)
ministry: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) — administrative control of NEDFi
agency: North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd (NEDFi), Gangtok and Namchi branches in Sikkim
subcategory: Rupee Term Loans for MSMEs and large projects; NEDFi Opportunity Scheme for Small Enterprises (NoSSE); Women Enterprise Development Scheme; Micro Lending Scheme (up to Rs.2 lakh); Micro Finance through MFIs/NGOs
period: Ongoing (NEDFi incorporated 1995; schemes operational and marketed in Sikkim through Gangtok and Namchi branches as of 2025-26)
whyItMatters: NEDFi is the region's development finance institution with physical branches in Gangtok and Namchi, actively disbursing to Sikkim homestays, traders and agri-allied units. For Sikkim entrepreneurs outside bank comfort zones, NEDFi's concessional windows (e.g., NoSSE loans up to Rs.1 crore at reported approx 8% p.a., women's enterprise loans, Rs.2-lakh micro loans) are the most accessible debt on offer. The State can multiply uptake via credit camps and by using NEDFi as a project-finance partner for tourism and organic-sector enterprises.
eligibleApplicants: MSMEs, entrepreneurs, women entrepreneurs, micro-borrowers and larger enterprises in the 8 NE states (private applicants; State role is facilitation)
sikkimNodalDept: Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Sikkim — likely
whatCanBeFunded: Setting up/expansion of industrial, infrastructure, agri-allied and service projects; working capital-linked term needs; micro-enterprise activity; women-led enterprise expansion, modernisation or diversification.
fundingAvailable: Scheme-dependent: NoSSE loans up to Rs.1 crore for projects between Rs.50 lakh and Rs.2 crore (reported approx 8% p.a., up to 7-year tenor); Micro Lending Scheme up to Rs.2 lakh per beneficiary; other windows per NEDFi published terms. No state quota.
fundingRatio: Not applicable (loans at concessional interest, repayable)
nePreferenceDetail: NEDFi lends only in the 8 NE states; NE-specific concessional pricing.
stateContribution: None; borrowers provide margin/security per scheme norms.
accessPathway: Entrepreneur approaches NEDFi Gangtok or Namchi branch (or applies via nedfi.com) with project proposal
Branch appraisal of eligibility, security and viability
Sanction and disbursement per scheme norms; repayment over agreed tenor
